segments.text: Welcome to your daily robotics and automation digest from July 18th, 2026.
Today we cover huge news, including the expanding Toyota-Nvidia AI partnership, new open robotics tools from Nvidia and Hugging Face, and advancements in physical AI through Fujitsu's collaboration.
From Robotics & Automation News, Toyota and Nvidia expand partnership to develop AI for vehicles, factories and cities.
This report details an expanded collaboration focusing on deploying Nvidia's computing, AI software, and simulation technologies across automotive, manufacturing, and urban planning sectors.

The partnership involves utilizing Nvidia's technologies to develop next-generation driver-assistance systems, accelerate software engineering through AI coding assistants, and create digital twins for factory simulations.
Additionally, the collaboration is being applied to urban mobility by using vision-language models for complex traffic analysis.
This work aims to establish the necessary AI infrastructure for autonomous vehicles, intelligent manufacturing, and responsive city environments.
The development signals a tangible progression toward integrating advanced artificial intelligence into physical world systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Nvidia and Hugging Face expand LeRobot with new open robotics AI tools.
This report details an expansion of the LeRobot platform through the integration of new artificial intelligence models and robotics frameworks.
The expansion involved incorporating Nvidia Isaac GR00T 1.7 and the Isaac Teleop framework to establish standardized workflows for data collection, training, and deployment in robotics applications.
Future plans include integrating Nvidia Cosmos 3 to provide access to world foundation models for synthetic data generation and policy development within the system.
This collaboration aims to increase accessibility to advanced physical AI technologies for the broader robotics community by leveraging existing Nvidia resources.
The integration is expected to accelerate the development of open-source robotics AI tools.
From Robotics & Automation News, Fujitsu partners with Fanuc, Yaskawa and Kawasaki to advance physical AI using Nvidia technology.
This collaboration aims to develop a collaborative control platform connecting digital systems with robots and physical equipment through the application of physical artificial intelligence.

The initiative involves integrating AI, robotics, simulation, and data analysis technologies into an open platform designed for interoperability and security across manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare sectors.
Fujitsu will leverage Nvidia's foundation models and Omniverse libraries to improve robot learning and simulation workflows within this framework established by the consortium.
This work seeks to address challenges related to labor shortages and aging workforces through the implementation of physical AI systems.
The resulting platform establishes a methodology for integrating complex operational data with physical robotic execution.
This development signals a pathway toward more tangible, real-world applications of advanced artificial intelligence in industrial settings.
From The Robot Report, Weave Robotics launches Isaac, its first mobile humanoid robot.
This story details the introduction of Isaac 1, a wheeled humanoid robot designed for household chores such as folding laundry and tidying rooms, demonstrating autonomous navigation capabilities.
The device features a friendly, soft exterior, adjustable height, and is controlled remotely through an application.
Isaac 1 operates on an eight-hour battery with a two-hour recharge time, and includes unique features like shutters on the head cameras to indicate operation and privacy screens for charging.
This robot is positioned as an affordable entry into home robotics via purchase or subscription models.
The development indicates a growing trend toward accessible domestic automation in the robotics sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, mimic Robotics unveils full-stack platform for dexterous robot manipulation.
This report details the introduction of a complete system designed to advance general-purpose dexterous manipulation for industrial robots through high-quality data collection.
The system incorporates the mimic hand M1, a tendon-driven robotic hand, and the mimic wearable U1 exoskeleton.
The design maintains a human hand morphology across hardware, data collection, and model training to mitigate cross-embodiment gaps.
Hardware components include force sensing, high backdrivability, and tactile sensors, managed by custom middleware to minimize latency.
This platform is intended to establish a general-purpose robotics foundation model for physical artificial intelligence.
The development signals a significant step toward creating versatile physical AI systems in industrial applications moving forward.
From latent.space, Kimi K3 launch shifts AI focus to efficiency stack.

This report details how the Kimi K3 demonstrated strong performance in coding and frontend tasks, challenging the compute moat thesis through advancements in methods like MoE routing and data curation.
Technical interest centered on the K3's utilization of Kimi Delta Attention for faster and cheaper context processing.
Benchmarks indicated that K3 achieved frontier-level results in coding agents and frontend evaluations by focusing computational resources efficiently.
The value is now perceived to reside in orchestration, memory architectures, and workflow scaffolding rather than solely in base model access.
Industry attention is now directed toward the development of these efficiency layers for future AI systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Agility Robotics opens new Fremont facility to accelerate physical AI development.

This report details the opening of a sixty thousand square foot facility in Fremont, California, which serves as the company's software and capabilities hub for training and testing AI technologies for its humanoid robot Digit.

The new site will house nearly two hundred employees across engineering and operations dedicated to driving next-generation AI capabilities within enterprise environments by leveraging Silicon Valley's AI talent ecosystem.
This expansion directly addresses customer demand for safer and more productive humanoid robots in logistics and manufacturing.
This development signals a tangible step forward in translating advanced artificial intelligence into practical, physical robotic applications.
From Robotics & Automation News, McLaren Construction to deploy autonomous robots at scale in partnership with FieldAI.
This report details the deployment of autonomous quadruped robots on UK construction sites to capture imagery, generate point cloud data, and perform progress verification against design models.
The collaboration involves utilizing FieldAI's AI foundation models, which enable the robots to adapt swiftly to complex, unstructured environments.
These robotic systems facilitate real-time monitoring of installation work, aiming to enhance quality control, reduce rework, and ensure compliance through deviation analysis.
This integration directly supports McLaren Construction's ongoing digital transformation strategy in the building sector.
The advancement signals a move toward integrating advanced AI for tangible quality assurance in large-scale physical environments.
From The Robot Report, "With new funding, Monumental plans to bring its construction robots to the U.S."
This segment details Monumental's recent financial success and expansion plans for its construction robotics technology.
Monumental secured thirty-two million dollars in Series B funding with the objective of expanding its deployment of construction robotics into the United States.
The company intends to utilize these funds for team growth, a U.S. market launch, and increased robot deployment across Europe.
These electric, autonomous robots employ sensors and artificial intelligence software to execute the precise laying of bricks and mortar on building sites.
Monumental operates within a subcontractor model, offering capacity while human operators maintain oversight of the complete construction workflow.
This development signals further integration of advanced robotics into the physical construction sector.
From The Robot Report, Founder of Maximo discusses how robotics is accelerating solar construction.

This report details how an AI-enabled robotics startup utilizes AI vision and robotics to automate the installation of solar modules, resulting in a faster, safer, and more efficient construction process.
Deise Yumi Asami, founder of Maximo, shared that the technology automates the placement of solar modules through advanced vision systems integrated with robotic systems on construction sites.
This methodology leverages AI vision for precise module positioning and robotics for automated installation tasks, significantly streamlining the deployment phase of solar energy infrastructure.

Asamini brought forward experience from scaling these innovative technologies within her parent company, The AES Corp., highlighting the practical application of these advancements in the energy sector.
This development indicates a trend toward increased integration of artificial intelligence and robotics within large-scale renewable energy infrastructure development.
From Robotics & Automation News, Robbyant releases LingBot-World 2.0 with hour-long real-time world generation.
This update introduces a new interactive world model capable of generating persistent environments over extended durations while maintaining visual quality and real-time interaction.
The system generates seventy-two-hundredp video at sixty frames per second and permits user control of characters through interfaces like Reactor.
It operates using a dual-agent architecture comprising a Pilot Agent and a Director Agent responsible for dynamic world evolution.
This advancement incorporates expanded interactive actions allowing for the triggering of events via text prompts, facilitating collaborative and persistent virtual environments.
The development signals a progression in creating complex, evolving simulations within artificial intelligence systems.

From Robotics & Automation News, Strider Robotics demonstrates a quadruped robot as commercial pilots begin, reporting that the system successfully carried a forty kilogram payload while maintaining stability across challenging terrain.
The demonstration involved a quadruped robot designed for demanding tasks utilizing an integrated artificial intelligence software platform for autonomous navigation and industrial inspection.

This research focuses on developing autonomous legged robotic systems paired with AI specifically for infrastructure monitoring, mining operations, and asset inspection in oil and gas and automotive sectors.
Strider Robotics is actively working with major clients to transition this technology from prototyping toward commercial deployment.
This development signals a shift toward practical application of advanced legged robotics in heavy industry and defense applications.
Further developments in this area are anticipated as the company pursues leadership in intelligent robotic systems.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Your Robot Surgeon Will See You Now"

shares weekly robotics videos and a calendar of upcoming robotics events concerning humanoid technology for laparoscopic surgery using a teleoperation framework, assessing its feasibility and challenges.
Research into this area evaluated humanoid systems employing a teleoperation framework to determine surgical feasibility and associated hurdles.
Further advancements include research on quadrupedal locomotion in complex environments introducing the APT-RL framework which enables high-speed, multi-skill movement.

New models such as Lumo-2 are being introduced for generalist embodied robot learning while other research explores biological systems achieving seamless transitions between air and water through wing and body kinematics.
This ongoing work signals progress in dexterous robotic manipulation and advanced locomotion systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Luyten opens early reservations for its Ascend A27 automated construction platform.

This report details the opening of early reservations for the Ascend A27 platform, which functions as a system to convert tower cranes into robotic systems capable of automated large-scale three-dimensional concrete printing.
The platform integrates robotics, artificial intelligence, and digital manufacturing processes to automate construction while leveraging existing crane infrastructure.
Early reservation customers receive priority access to production and an introductory offer with deposits credited toward the final price.
This development expands Luyten's offering into larger vertical construction applications beyond their established three-dimensional printing capabilities.
The advancement signals further integration of advanced robotics into heavy industry and construction sectors.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, This Graduate Student Equips NASA’s Robots With Assembly Skills.
This story details a development of an algorithm enabling robots to install satellite antennas with precise positioning.

The work involved a graduate student named Sarah Downs collaborating with NASA and the United States Air Force to create an algorithm that allows robotic systems to correctly position antennas on satellites in space.
The developed algorithm provides the necessary instructions for these robots to execute accurate assembly tasks in the space environment.
This achievement successfully equips NASA's robots with essential assembly skills through advanced algorithmic programming.
This advancement demonstrates the growing capability of artificial intelligence in facilitating complex, remote robotic operations across aerospace applications.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Jon Roberts of Inteq: ‘The software layer is where automation investment is won or lost’"
reports on the critical role of the software layer in determining the success of automation investments.
The interview highlights that Warehouse Execution Systems function as the central intelligence connecting physical hardware and human workflows for unified control.
This perspective indicates a shift away from hardware-led strategies toward software-first approaches to achieve greater flexibility and adaptability in response to changing operational requirements.
Autonomous Mobile Robots are established as core infrastructure, increasingly supported by models such as Robotics-as-a-Service.
Achieving predictive operations driven by artificial intelligence necessitates a robust orchestration platform that provides real-time visibility across all integrated systems and data streams.
Future success in the automation sector depends on developing hardware-agnostic software platforms that facilitate seamless and flexible expansion.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Scott Zerkle of Panasonic Connect: ‘AI is only as good as the data it receives’"

This report details the current application and future trajectory of artificial intelligence within electronics manufacturing, highlighting that AI's primary value currently lies in predictive maintenance and defect detection supporting human workers.
The future of smart manufacturing involves integrating data from machines, materials, and processes to allow factories to learn and improve based on production history.
Component miniaturization demands highly precise printing and placement that must adapt in real time.
Automation assists in balancing quality, throughput, and resilience by monitoring the five Ms of manufacturing: human, machine, material, method, and measurement.
The major upcoming shift involves the convergence of artificial intelligence, sensing, and automation to form interconnected, self-optimizing manufacturing ecosystems.
This development signals a move toward fully integrated, adaptive factory environments driven by comprehensive data streams.
From Robotics & Automation News, Aetina adds support for Nvidia Jetson T3000 and T2000 AI modules.
This report details Aetina's plan to expand its portfolio by supporting the new Nvidia Jetson T3000 and T2000 AI modules for robotics and industrial edge artificial intelligence applications.
Aetina intends to integrate these modules into its upcoming DeviceEdge AIE-KT and AIE-PT fan-based and fanless systems, respectively.
The Jetson T3000 module offers up to 865 FP4 TFLOPS at a power consumption of 70 watts, while the T2000 provides up to 400 FP4 TFLOPS suitable for applications such as autonomous robots.
This integration enables hardware families to facilitate scaling robotics projects across development and production phases.
Nvidia forecasts module availability in the first quarter of 2027 along with full support for the associated AI software ecosystem.
This expansion positions Aetina to enhance the capabilities of edge AI systems in the industrial sector.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "The Download: perimenopause misinformation and China’s latest AI leap"
This story examines the intersection of health misinformation regarding perimenopause and recent technological advancements in artificial intelligence.
Developments detailed include China's progress in open artificial intelligence models and research into brain implants.
Further topics addressed privacy concerns related to period tracking devices and innovations in converting waste materials into agricultural resources.
The report also discusses societal impacts stemming from social media monetization and facial recognition technology.
This content integrates health awareness with substantial technological breakthroughs.
The ongoing development in AI and neurotechnology signals continued shifts in both public health discourse and technological application across various sectors.

From refer.tldr.tech, TLDR AI Daily AI News for Technical Readers is a free daily newsletter that delivers AI news, research, and tools in a quick five-minute read summarizing model releases, research papers, and new tools with links to the sources.
This publication serves engineers, researchers, and technical professionals by providing dense and focused technical signals regarding advancements in artificial intelligence.

The service maintains a subscriber base of one million one hundred thousand and disseminates updates every weekday focusing on the summarization of specific model releases and technical findings from the research community.
The content emphasizes engineering-focused information rather than broad coverage, aiming to provide deep technical context for the AI landscape.
This focus indicates an ongoing trend toward highly specialized and technically granular dissemination of AI developments within the professional community.
From The Tech Buzz, "Beyond Tech: Your Weekend Upgrade"
This segment covers consumer technology highlights including an electric vehicle sales rebound, the release of iOS 27 with new Siri AI features, and novel OpenAI hardware such as a speaker.
The reporting also addresses trends in art and culture, noting a backlash against artificial intelligence in film, alongside developments in sports concerning World Cup robotics.
Further wellness trends involve Biogen drugs and AI diagnostics, while food trends focus on the return on investment for AI in the food and beverage sector.
A related strategy discussed involves scaling external traffic beyond pay-per-click advertising by emphasizing proven channel attribution methods.
These developments indicate a continuing integration of artificial intelligence across consumer goods, entertainment, and health sectors.
From thehustle.co, "Monk wine booming amidst falling booze sales"
This report examines the performance of wine produced by British monks and its success despite a decline in overall alcohol sales.
The monk-made wine is noted as a successful product within the context of a general freefall in alcohol market figures.
Reports indicate that this specific category of wine has maintained or increased market traction while broader alcohol consumption experiences a contraction across various sectors.

This niche success contrasts with wider economic trends involving advancements in artificial intelligence, tourism development, and emerging business ventures such as various startups and the economics of amusement parks.
Furthermore, developments in biotech protein creation are also noted within this broader context.
The focus remains on localized market success amidst larger industry shifts in technology and consumption patterns.
From thehustle.co, "Fragrance Clubs Become New Social Connections"
This report details the emergence of fragrance clubs as a novel method for social connection by transforming the individual experience of smelling into a collective activity.
These clubs manifest in various formats such as blind-sniff meetups, workshops, and fragrance swaps, currently operating in metropolitan areas including Los Angeles, Berlin, and Shanghai.
This trend is fueled by a growing fragrance industry interest among Generation Z and a documented desire for in-person socialization.

The clubs establish community through shared sensory experiences focused on emotional evocation rather than technical knowledge, functioning similarly to established book or wine clubs with open invitations.
This phenomenon indicates a consumer shift toward experiential social engagement within the wellness and lifestyle sectors.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope your algorithms are running smoothly.
Until tomorrow, keep innovating and enjoy the ride!
See you then.
